result.title: LoRazor: Trimming Adapter Execution for Efficient Multi-LoRA Serving
result.summary: LoRA offers a parameter-efficient adaptation strategy, supporting multi-user workloads via customized adapters on a shared backbone. However, serving concurrent requests with different adapters introduces substantial computation and memory-management overhead. We ask the research question: Do all requests need their adapters throughout the whole generation process? Our motivational study reveals that employing LoRA adapters at every decoding step is unnecessary, releasing them early has limited impact on accuracy while substantially accelerating generation. Although skipping adapters early offers theoretical workload reduction, translating these computational savings into concrete throughput gains requires tailored GPU kernels. We present LoRazor, a multi-LoRA serving framework that combines early adapter release with active-row aware GPU kernels. LoRazor determines when to permanently release a request's adapter and continue decoding with the backbone alone. By dynamically resizing LoRA kernel launches as adapters are released, LoRazor trims idle GPU blocks. Across two backbones and four tasks, LoRazor achieves up to 3.02x request throughput and 2.53x output-token throughput over vLLM multi-LoRA, with a mean relative task-accuracy decrease of 2.89%.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究多 LoRA 并发服务的效率问题，发现生成后期不再需要适配器，提出提前永久释放适配器并配合活跃行感知 GPU kernel 来裁剪冗余计算，在精度小幅下降的前提下显著提升吞吐。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「何时停止依赖额外计算分支」的判定与精度–计算量权衡曲线，可能为 LVR 中的停止决策与动态算力分配提供类比线索，但属服务系统层面优化，迁移性需核查。
